Root Finding: Solving Equations¶

A root of f is a value x with f(x) = 0. Pluss solves scalar equations in batches: every solver advances all lanes of a Series together with ordinary array operations, so one call solves a single equation or a whole parameter sweep with a different equation in each lane. After this chapter you can pick a method, set its stopping rules, solve many equations at once, check that a root is real, and differentiate a root with respect to a parameter.

Every program is complete and its output is the output of that program.

The solvers¶

All live in pluss::subsp::math::roots. f is a std::function<Series(const Series&)> that maps a Series of any shape to a Series of the same shape.

Solver

Needs

Idea

bisect(f, lo, hi)

a bracket: f(lo), f(hi) of opposite signs

halve each lane’s interval; slow but certain

illinois(f, a, b)

a bracket

regula falsi with the Illinois correction; superlinear, never leaves the bracket

newton(f, x, df)

a start, optionally the derivative

Newton–Raphson; df empty uses a central difference

secant(f, x0, x1)

two starts

derivative-free, superlinear

householder(evaluate, x)

a start, and f with its first three derivatives

fourth-order iteration; its root also carries sensitivities

Options is {max_iterations, x_tolerance, f_tolerance, check_every, derivative_step} with defaults {100, 0, 0, 8, 1e-6}. A tolerance of 0 means “off”: with both off, all max_iterations run. With a tolerance set, the solver stops once every lane meets it, checked every check_every iterations (set it to 1 for the earliest stop; checking costs a host synchronisation, which is why it is not done every time).

Result holds root, residual (f at the root), iterations, and bracketed (false when some lane of a bracketed solver had no sign change).

Programs¶

  • Solving equations

Checklist¶

  1. With a bracket, start with illinois; use bisect when you must be certain.

  2. Without one, newton (analytic derivative if you have it), or secant.

  3. Set f_tolerance or x_tolerance to stop early; lower check_every for the earliest stop.

  4. Read bracketed and residual before trusting a root.

  5. Put the whole sweep in one Series; do not loop over equations yourself.
